test_title: SSC Steno 2022 Official Paper (Held On: 17 Nov 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Radha told her friends that / she will discuss the project / with her mentor when / she would meet him tomorrow.
solution:
The erroneous part is **'she would meet him tomorrow'.****​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in '**she would meet him tomorrow.**' When we are talking about the future within a time clause, we use the present tense, not the future.
 
• The segment '**Radha told her friends that**' is grammatically correct. It properly starts off the sentence by introducing the subject (Radha) and what she is doing (telling her friends).
 
• '**She will discuss the project**' is also grammatically correct as it follows the rule of reported speech where the present tense in the directly reported speech is converted to the future tense in the indirect speech.
 
• '**With her mentor when**' is also grammatically correct. It conveys who Radha is discussing the project with and also introduces a time clause.
 
• Hence, the correct segment should be '**she meets him tomorrow.**'

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Time clauses are used to indicate the time of an action. They often come after conjunctions like when, before, after, as soon as, etc. In time clauses, even when we are talking about future events, we use the present simple or present perfect tense rather than future tense.
 
• This English grammar rule is known as 'future in the past.'
